s: Paris's oldest covered market (1628), tucked down a quiet Marais side street
w: Behind an unassuming doorway, Paris's oldest surviving covered market has been trading since 1628. The hall holds a handful of excellent food stalls and tiny communal-table restaurants -- cheese, charcuterie, fresh pasta, Moroccan tagines -- more neighbourhood regulars than tourist crowd. Small, warm, and unpretentious.
_facts: Located on Rue de Bretagne in the Marais, 3rd arrondissement
Trading since 1628 -- the oldest covered market in Paris
Houses food stalls and small restaurants with shared seating
Named for a former orphanage on the site whose children wore red
